title: Serialize concurrent switchProject calls
body:
## Summary
Two overlapping switchProject calls finish in the order their touch POSTs return, not the order the user clicked.

## Description
src/stores/projectStore.ts switchProject awaits saveToRecent, transitionProject and the touch POST before it sets identity, with no ticket. The second click can complete first, so the first click wins the final identity. The loadProgress guard keeps progress consistent with the last load, but identity order is still response order.

## Flow
- click recent project B, then C before B touch returns
- C touch returns first, identity C, then B returns, identity B
- user sees B after choosing C

## Expected impact
The last project clicked is the one opened. A ticket could drop a switch the user still expected if the newer one fails.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - last click wins
Before: no test; 3 walked orderings, 1 ends on the wrong project
After: 0 of 3 wrong
Method: simulation - deferred fetch test not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/stores/projectStore.ts switchProject: await Promise.all, await apiFetch touch, then set() with no recheck
instrument: deferred-fetch vitest: two switchProject calls, resolve touches out of order, assert projectPath is the last target

title: Queue a forced scan that arrives during a running scan
body:
## Summary
scanProject({force:true}) returns immediately when a scan is running, so a post-run re-check can read pre-run files.

## Description
src/stores/projectStore.ts scanProject checks isScanning before force. useSectionScaffold.ts:46 and :69 force a scan to see files a run just wrote, and useFileWatcher.ts:127 starts scans on the same writes, so the two collide. The forced caller .finally() re-grades against the old dynamicContext.

## Flow
- run writes files
- file watcher starts a scan
- useSectionScaffold forces a scan, which returns early
- section re-grades on a result that may predate the files

## Expected impact
Post-run grades reflect the files the run wrote, at one extra scan per collision.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - force means fresh
Before: force during a scan issues 0 requests (code read)
After: force during a scan issues 1 follow-up request and its promise waits for it
Method: simulation - needs a deferred-fetch test and a queue design
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: scan in flight, call force, assert fetch count 2 and that the forced promise resolves after the second response

title: Key the scan cache by project path
body:
## Summary
dynamicContext carries no project identity, so the 5-minute cache can serve one project to another that was set without a flip.

## Description
scanProject trusts dynamicContext.scannedAt only. Flips through transitionProject clear it, but SetupWizard.tsx:151,163,173,182 call setProject with a new projectPath and leave dynamicContext alone, so re-picking a project in the wizard keeps the earlier scan as fresh.

## Flow
- wizard picks A and a scan lands
- user goes back and picks B
- scanProject sees a fresh scannedAt and returns
- prompts carry A classes for up to 5 minutes

## Expected impact
Prompt context always matches the open project, at one extra scan after a re-pick.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - context matches project
Before: 1 of 1 walked wizard re-pick serves the old scan
After: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - whether any scan runs during the wizard needs a component walk
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/stores/projectStore.ts scanProject cache check on dynamicContext?.scannedAt
src/components/modules/project-setup/SetupWizard.tsx:151,163,173,182
instrument: store test: dynamicContext scanned for A, setProject path B, assert scanProject issues a fetch; plus a check that the wizard can reach a scan

title: Remove lifecycle and bus exports with zero consumers
body:
## Summary
Five exported helpers have no caller in src, e2e or scripts, tests included.

## Description
composeLifecycles and createSubscriptionLifecycle (src/lib/lifecycle.ts), EventBus.replayTo and clearReplayBuffer (src/lib/event-bus.ts), getProgressOwner (src/services/ProjectModuleBridge.ts). .claude/CLAUDE.md names createSubscriptionLifecycle as a factory and the bus header promises replay for late subscribers while nothing replays, so the docs need the same change.

## Flow
- delete the five exports
- update .claude/CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture
- run typecheck

## Expected impact
About 60 fewer lines and docs that describe what runs. Out-of-tree callers would break; none are known.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dead surface removed
Before: 5 exports, 0 consumers
After: 0 exports
Method: probe - git grep over src e2e scripts; deletion not applied because docs are director-owned
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: git grep -lw over src e2e scripts returned nothing for composeLifecycles, createSubscriptionLifecycle, replayTo, clearReplayBuffer; getProgressOwner appears only in its own file
instrument: typecheck failing paths after deletion, plus a docs grep for the removed names

title: Decide moduleHealth and moduleHistory: zero writers, still persisted
body:
## Summary
updateHealth and addHistoryEntry have no production caller, yet both fields are persisted, POSTed on every save and loaded back.

## Description
src/stores/moduleStore.ts updateHealth and addHistoryEntry have no call site outside tests; ModuleShell/index.tsx:160 already says updateHealth has zero call sites. Readers only ever see empty or legacy data. Either wire a writer or retire the fields from the store, the POST body and the project_progress row.

## Flow
- owner picks wire or retire
- if retiring, drop the actions, the partialize keys and the body fields
- leave stored rows readable

## Expected impact
Removes state that looks live but is not. Retiring touches a stored row shape, so it needs an owner call.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - state has a writer or is gone
Before: 2 fields, 0 production writers
After: 0 writerless fields
Method: probe - git grep for both action names outside tests and the store
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence: src/stores/moduleStore.ts:110; src/components/modules/ModuleShell/index.tsx:160 comment; git grep updateHealth and addHistoryEntry outside __tests__ and moduleStore

title: Server-side eval.visual emit reaches no subscriber
body:
## Summary
The verify/visual route emits on the in-process bus, but the only listener that could see it is a browser devtools panel in another process.

## Description
src/app/api/verify/visual/route.ts:186 emits eval.visual from a route handler. git grep finds no eventBus.on for that channel, and onAny lives in the client EventBusDevTools. The event sits in a server replay buffer and reaches nobody, so the emit reads as a notification that does not exist.

## Flow
- POST /api/verify/visual
- route emits eval.visual on the server bus
- no server subscriber, and the browser bus is a different instance

## Expected impact
A real delivery path or an honest removal. A removal could drop a planned integration.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - emits have a receiver
Before: 1 server emit with 0 receivers
After: 0 receiverless emits
Method: probe - grep of every eventBus.on, onNamespace and onAny site
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/app/api/verify/visual/route.ts:186; subscriber sites DispatchHealthPanel, toastHandler, EventBusDevTools, useActivityFeedBridge, event-bus-bridge, gate-notifier (none on eval.visual)
instrument: route test asserting either a named delivery path fires or no emit occurs

title: Back onto an entry with no g param leaves the URL unnamed
body:
## Summary
useActiveGameUrlSync popstate ignores an absent g, so the store stays on a non-default game while the URL names none.

## Description
src/stores/activeGameStore.ts onPop adopts only a valid g. gameUrl leaves g absent for the default game, so an older entry has no g. Going Back onto it keeps the current game with no rewrite. Fixed means writeGame runs on that branch, or absent adopts the default; which one is a product read.

## Flow
- open / with default game
- switch to gtai, which replaces g on the current entry
- navigate, then Back to an entry without g
- store says gtai, URL has no g

## Expected impact
The address always names the game shown, on a low-traffic path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - URL names the game
Before: 1 walked Back case ends with no g while the game is non-default
After: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - needs a jsdom popstate test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/stores/activeGameStore.ts onPop: const g = parseGameParam(window.location.search); if (g && g !== current) setGame(g)
instrument: jsdom test: store on gtai, pushState a URL without g, dispatch popstate, assert g=gtai or the store on default

title: saveToRecent reads checklist counts without checking the owner
body:
## Summary
The recent-projects row takes whatever checklist is in memory, even when it belongs to no project or another one.

## Description
projectStore.saveToRecent calls getChecklistProgress() with no owner check, and completeSetup runs it before loadProgress, so an existing project is saved with empty or stale counts until a later save. getProgressOwner exists in the bridge for this and has no caller.

## Flow
- open an existing project through setup
- completeSetup saves to recent first
- row records counts before the project progress loaded
- recent list shows wrong done/total

## Expected impact
The recent list shows real progress, by changing one call order.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - recent counts match the project
Before: 1 walked setup path saves before load
After: load precedes save on that path
Method: simulation - requires a test across completeSetup and the recent route
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/stores/projectStore.ts completeSetup and saveToRecent; src/services/ProjectModuleBridge.ts getProgressOwner (no consumers)
instrument: store test: non-new project, completeSetup, assert the save body carries the loaded counts
